summary: Today's biggest opening is EASD 2026 (Milan, Sep 28–Oct 2). Several diabetes and GLP-1 abstracts under embargo are already out, and the rest of the meeting will land this week. Before it starts, the best pre-positioning picks are the UK Biobank study on ultra-processed food, activity and type 2 diabetes by genetic risk, and the orforglipron menopause-stage analysis. The second big hook is seasonal: TikTok's 'Winter Arc' challenge starts Oct 1, and NYT covered it today. An evidence-based 'Winter Arc that actually works' is a strong early play, as long as it avoids extreme dieting. Fresh ESC/NEJM cardiology items are also worth covering, with careful absolute-number framing: the CTX310 CRISPR one-shot LDL phase 1 and the SINGLE-AF trial (69% relative, 1.5%→0.5% absolute). Caveats: the glucosamine–Alzheimer's story is a June Nature Metabolism study that ScienceDaily re-surfaced. It's observational plus mouse data, so it's an association-only explainer. The tirzepatide brown-fat story is mice only. The oral-vs-transdermal HRT clot story is still our strongest carry-over (88→86), and the SELECT mediation story holds steady. REM sleep and measles are now peaking. The Galleri and REFIT2 stories are slowing. Google Trends and Wikipedia had no health-specific spikes today (all sports, politics and entertainment).

candidates.topic: Menopause HRT pills vs patches/gels and blood clots: ~1 extra serious clot per 1,000 women/year on oral; no overall increase with transdermal (The BMJ, Danish nationwide nested case-control, women 50–69)
candidates.angle: 'Same hormone, different road': why swallowing estrogen vs absorbing it through skin changes clot risk (first-pass liver effect). Give absolute numbers first, relative second. End with questions to bring to your clinician, not a switch recommendation.
candidates.why_now: Seen in 3+ snapshots with momentum holding at 86–88. Menopause content is booming on TikTok/IG, and there's a clear practical question. Coverage is still mostly news write-ups, not creator explainers.

evidence.signal: Tracked across multiple snapshots at 82–88 momentum; BMJ published Sep 23, 2026

candidates.topic: Ultra-processed food + 150 min/week activity cut type 2 diabetes risk by 49–70% regardless of genetic risk (UK Biobank, 56,964 adults, EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: 'Your genes aren't your destiny': the combined effect held in high, intermediate and low genetic-risk groups. Be clear about what it measured (each +10% of diet by weight from UPF → 7% higher risk). It's observational, and the cohort's average age was 69.5.
keywords: can you prevent type 2 diabetes if it runs in your family
candidates.why_now: The embargo lifted Sep 26, ahead of EASD, which starts tomorrow. It overlaps with The Independent's UPF report coverage. Few creator videos yet.

evidence.signal: 56,964 UK Biobank adults, 926 cases over 7.8 years; +7% risk per 10% UPF; activity −39%; combined −49/−70/−59% by genetic risk; authors note observational limits
New report on serious risks of ultra-processed foods, Sep 25

candidates.topic: The science-backed 'Winter Arc': what 90-day habit research actually says (TikTok challenge starts Oct 1)
candidates.angle: Ride the viral trend with evidence. Habit formation takes a median of about 66 days, with a wide range. Pick 2–3 keystone habits (sleep regularity, strength training, hourly movement breaks, daylight). Skip the cold-plunge and extreme-diet parts. The anti-hype 'what actually works' version.
keywords: how long to form a habit
candidates.why_now: The NYT ran 'Are You Ready for Your Winter Arc?' today. The challenge officially starts Oct 1. Search demand ramps sharply in the last week of September. Most existing content is motivational, not evidence-based.

evidence.signal: 'Are You Ready for Your Winter Arc?' published Sep 27
2026 Winter Arc runs Oct 1–Dec 31; billions of TikTok views in 2025
Hourly 5-minute movement breaks improved mood and fatigue (11,484 participants), a ready evidence-backed habit

candidates.topic: One CRISPR infusion (CTX310) cut LDL cholesterol ~52% and triglycerides ~48% for a full year (phase 1, 15 patients, NEJM / ESC 2026)
candidates.angle: 'A one-time cholesterol fix?' Explain how switching off ANGPTL3 in the liver works. Be honest: phase 1, 15 people with hard-to-treat lipid disorders, 15-year follow-up required. Say what it means (and doesn't) for everyday statin users.
candidates.why_now: ScienceDaily pickup today, following NEJM/ESC. 'One-time cure' framing is about to spread on social, so we get there early with the accurate version.

evidence.signal: Phase 1, 15 patients; 52.5% LDL and 47.8% triglyceride reduction at 12 months (highest dose); no related serious adverse events

candidates.topic: Glucosamine joint supplement linked to 25% higher odds of MCI progressing to dementia (Nature Metabolism; observational records + mouse/brain-tissue data)
candidates.angle: 'Should you worry about your joint supplement?' Walk through what was found (association in 2,750 MCI patients, 8% users), why it isn't proof, the proposed glycosylation mechanism from mice, and questions for your doctor. Also: what the joint-pain evidence for glucosamine even looks like.
candidates.why_now: ScienceDaily re-surfaced it today. Supplement-safety content drives saves and shares for 45+ viewers. Note the paper was published June 2026, so present it as 'resurfacing', not brand-new.

evidence.signal: 1,896 AD + 2,750 MCI records; 25% higher likelihood of progression; authors say it doesn't show causation, and an RCT is needed
Hyperglycosylation is a metabolic driver of Alzheimer's disease (original paper, June 2026)
Prior mainstream coverage in June, so competition is moderate

candidates.topic: Weight loss explains only ~20% of semaglutide's heart benefit (SELECT mediation analysis, European Heart Journal)
candidates.angle: 'It's not (just) the weight.' What else GLP-1s might do for the heart, plus the new Diabetes Care predictors-of-weight-loss paper from the same trial. Tie it to the EASD week news cycle.
candidates.why_now: Steady across 4 snapshots, and there's a new companion SELECT paper in Diabetes Care (Sep 24). EASD will add a fresh wave of GLP-1 news.

evidence.signal: Predictors of Peak Body Weight Loss With Semaglutide in the SELECT Trial (Sep 24)

candidates.topic: Oral GLP-1 orforglipron: similar weight loss (up to ~14%) in pre-, peri- and postmenopausal women (ATTAIN-1/2 post-hoc, EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: 'Does menopause blunt GLP-1 weight loss?' The data says results were similar across stages. Note it's a post-hoc analysis with 142–225 women per group, and the pill isn't a replacement for anything you're prescribed.
candidates.why_now: EASD embargo lifted Sep 26. It merges two hot audience themes, menopause and GLP-1 pills, and almost no creators have covered it yet.

evidence.signal: Post-hoc of ATTAIN-1/2; up to 14% weight loss; 83% vs 30% placebo achieved ≥5%; similar across menopausal stages at 72 weeks

candidates.topic: Your smartwatch may overestimate calories burned, and the error grows with body fat percentage (PLOS One, 4 watches vs metabolic cart)
candidates.angle: 'Don't eat back your watch calories.' What wearables measure well (heart rate, steps) and what they don't (energy expenditure), limited to activity calories.
keywords: should I eat back exercise calories
candidates.why_now: Seen in 3 snapshots with momentum growing (72→74). Medical Xpress picked it up Sep 26. Very shareable, low creator coverage so far.

evidence.signal: 'The higher your body fat percentage, the less accurate your smartwatch is at measuring calories burned'

candidates.topic: Type 2 diabetes: combined risk of kidney disease, heart failure or death reaches 33% at 5 years and 55% at 10 years after diagnosis (1.6M US patients, EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: The 'silent decade' after a type 2 diagnosis. Which checks matter early (kidney urine test, eGFR, blood pressure) and why guidelines now push early organ protection. Present the combined endpoint honestly; the numbers aren't only deaths.
candidates.why_now: EASD embargo release Sep 26, and the conference news cycle runs all week.

evidence.signal: 1.6M+ US patients; combined CKD/HF/death risk 33% at 5 years, 55% at 10 years

candidates.topic: Flu season 2026–27: new mRNA flu shot for 50+, subclade K, and 'when should I get it / how long does it last?'
candidates.angle: The timing question answered with CDC guidance: protection wanes over months, so September–October is the usual target window. What's new this year for adults 50+.
keywords: how long does flu shot last
candidates.why_now: The seasonal cycle is starting. Detroit Free Press 'How long does flu shot last?' shows the exact question people are searching. Roche Xofluza generic licensing in STAT.

evidence.signal: 'How long does flu shot last? What experts say this fall', Sep 25

candidates.topic: Hourly 5-minute walk breaks improved mood and fatigue without hurting work performance (BJSM, 11,484 people) + a 10-minute slow jog sharpened focus (24 adults)
candidates.angle: 'The smallest workout that still counts.' Stack two new studies, but rank them by evidence strength: the large pragmatic trial first, the small 24-person lab study second. Make the payoff a desk-worker protocol.
keywords: how often should you get up from your desk

candidates.topic: Blood thinners for 'intermediate-risk' atrial fibrillation: SINGLE-AF RCT found a 69% relative reduction in combined stroke/bleeding/CV death (1.5% → 0.5%; NEJM, 1,803 Korean patients)
candidates.angle: The AFib 'gray zone' explained: what the CHA2DS2-VASc score is, what this trial changes, and why the absolute difference is 1 percentage point. No drug or dosing advice; it's a conversation starter with your cardiologist.
keywords: do I need a blood thinner for AFib
candidates.why_now: ScienceDaily pickup today of an NEJM RCT. AFib is common in the 50+ audience. Near-zero creator coverage.

evidence.signal: RCT, 1,803 patients, 18 Korean centers; primary endpoint 0.5% vs 1.5%; open-label

candidates.why_now: BMJ news piece (Sep 25) is keeping it alive, but momentum is decaying (80→74→66). Still worth covering with a consumer-decision angle.

candidates.topic: Mounjaro/Zepbound (tirzepatide) may switch on calorie-burning brown fat, but only in mice so far (Biomedicine & Pharmacotherapy)
candidates.angle: 'Is there more to tirzepatide than appetite?' Pair-fed mouse design shown simply. Hard stop on 'mice ≠ humans'. A myth-buster Short that pre-empts overhyped TikToks.
